function: Learns joint active beamforming at the HAP and passive IRS phase shifts with DDPG; resource allocation and IRS association are solved by optimization (p. 6).
system: Reflecting IRSs (L=4, M=64 elements each) assist an N=4-antenna HAP and K=4 single-antenna devices in wireless-powered MEC at 3 GHz (pp. 3, 10).
method: Reinforcement learning with DDPG (actor-critic, fully connected DNN with two hidden layers), trained by interaction with the simulated environment; upper layer is optimization-based (pp. 6, 8).
data_channel: Own simulator: all channels randomly generated following the Rayleigh distribution; no measured data or standard model; the agent learns in the same simulated environment (p. 10).
test_conditions: Default Table II setting (K=L=N=4, M=64, Pmax=30 dBm, p. 10); parameter sweeps over K, N, M, Pmax, device CPU rate (pp. 11-13); no unseen scenario reported.
baselines: Non-learned: without IRS, random IRS association, random IRS configuration, AO like [42], exhaustive search, offloading only, local computing only; learned: DQN beamforming like [41] (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Energy cost utility (data processed per energy cost, Mbits/J), reward convergence over steps, running time in ms (pp. 5, 11-13).
complexity: Order of complexity O(I(KL + network-size terms)) (p. 10); measured runtime about 34 ms versus 680-982 ms for the AO algorithm (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 10: "following the Rayleigh distribution"; custom simulator with Rayleigh fading, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "the dimension of the state space is 2K"; network size depends on K, N, M, L, so each sweep point needs its own network; no unseen-scenario test or adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 10: "DQN-Learning-Based Beamforming" (learned, like [41]) and "Random IRS Configuration" (non-learned); p. 12: "outperforms the DQN-optimization scheme" in energy cost utility (Fig. 9).
q4_support: p. 10: "the complexity of the proposed hierarchical optimization framework is" an explicit O(...) expression; p. 13: "consistently maintains a running time of around 34 ms".
q5_support: p. 10: "we randomly generate the channel matrix"; simulated Rayleigh channels, and the paper gives no link to code or data anywhere.
notes: Included: the learned element is the DDPG active and passive beamforming (area 3, physical layer); offloading, energy, computation and IRS association are solved by classical optimization (Dinkelbach, matching), so above_phy does not apply. First page holds the title and DOI. Table II (p. 10) and Figs. 5-13 were read as page images.
